messages.subject: file monitor reactives
parts:
Hi,

  That is triggered by the shiny runloop and fires when the file changes?

-Alex

messages.author: c8fe4075ec631c03
messages.subject: Re: file monitor reactives
parts:
okay, it's very useful to wrap these functions up, since I can see using poll, certainly.

In general I'm now feeling it would be great to get some of the more profound use cases wrapped up in a standard or example implementation - coordinating writes to a single file or database for multi-user interaction with a core dataset seems pretty important and I'm no idea how it might work in the reactive model.  I'm prepared to be astonished by how elegant it tuns out to be, but right now I'm guessing.

The solutions above do polling, and I'm looking in another direction at the moment - I want to build asynchrony into shiny by allowing it to spawn jobs using R parallel and system fork/exec, and then get the results back in the following ways:

  a reactive that triggers when it gets the signal that the child has finished.  Using ... wait?
  a reactive that triggers when a file gets updated (for larger results or ones where R would have to write it back to the FS first anyway (e.g. images)  using select()
  a side reactive that monitors stderr to read progress from long running jobs.  Using select()

-Alex
